title: SQS, SNS and EventBridge: queue, topic and event bus

videos.script: Lesson 20 ended with work that should not happen inside a request. This lesson is about where that work waits. {{handoff}} Three services do it, and they are easy to confuse. A queue holds messages until a consumer takes them. A topic copies one message to every subscriber. A bus reads each event and lets rules decide where it goes. {{shapes}} You will start with the queue, and the detail that surprises people. Receiving a message does not remove it. It hides it. You will watch one message come back three times, and then move to a dead-letter queue on its own. {{redrive}} Then a topic that feeds two teams, one of them through a filter. Then a bus that sends large orders to review and drops the rest. {{fanout}} Last, the promise every queue breaks sooner or later. A message can arrive twice. A FIFO queue narrows that. A consumer that remembers what it has done makes it harmless, and you will run one. {{dupes}}
